translations.idiomatic: Yue said to Minister Li Shi, "It would be better to reserve a place for the Imperial Primordial Ancestor without identifying it with any particular person.

sentences.zh: 」時大喜，告璁。

translations.literal: " Shi was greatly pleased and told Cong.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Shi was greatly pleased and told Zhang Cong.

sentences.zh: 璁不謂然，以初議上。

translations.literal: Cong did not agree and submitted the original proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong did not agree and submitted the original proposal.

sentences.zh: 帝竟令題皇初祖主，如嶽言。

translations.literal: The emperor ultimately ordered the tablet inscribed "Imperial Primordial Ancestor," as Yue had said.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ultimately ordered the tablet inscribed with the title Imperial Primordial Ancestor, just as Yue had advised.

sentences.zh: 璁銜之，出為廣西提學僉事。

translations.literal: Cong harbored resentment; Yue was sent out as education intendant vice commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong harbored resentment, and Yue was sent out to serve as education intendant vice commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 行部柳州，軍缺餉大嘩，城閉五日。

translations.literal: On tour in Liuzhou, the troops lacked pay and raised a great uproar; the city was closed for five days.
translations.idiomatic: While on tour in Liuzhou, the troops went unpaid and raised a great uproar; the city gates were shut for five days.

sentences.zh: 嶽令守城啟門，召詰嘩者予餉去。

translations.literal: Yue ordered the garrison to open the gate, summoned and questioned the rioters, gave them pay, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Yue ordered the garrison to open the gates, summoned the rioters for questioning, paid them their arrears, and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 尋以計擒首惡，置之理。

translations.literal: Soon by stratagem he captured the ringleaders and placed them before the law.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, by stratagem, he captured the ringleaders and brought them to justice.

sentences.zh: 入賀，改提學江西。

translations.literal: On entering court to offer congratulations, he was transferred to education intendant of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered court to offer congratulations, he was transferred to education intendant of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 不謝璁，璁黜廣西選貢七人，謫嶽廣東鹽課提舉。

translations.literal: He did not thank Cong; Cong dismissed seven selected tribute students of Guangxi and demoted Yue to salt tax intendant of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Because he did not thank Zhang Cong, Cong dismissed seven selected tribute students from Guangxi and demoted Yue to salt tax intendant of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 遷廉州知府。

translations.literal: Promoted to prefect of Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 督民墾棄地，教以桔槔運水。

translations.literal: He supervised the people in reclaiming abandoned land and taught them to use the shaduf to transport water.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the people in reclaiming abandoned land and taught them to irrigate it with shadufs.

sentences.zh: 廉民多盜珠池。

translations.literal: The people of Lian often stole from the pearl pools.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Lianzhou often poached from the pearl pools.

sentences.zh: 岳居四年，未嘗入一珠。

translations.literal: Yue lived there four years and never entered a single pearl pool.
translations.idiomatic: Yue lived there four years and never once entered a pearl pool.

sentences.zh: 帝使使往安南詰莫登庸殺主，岳言于總督張經曰：「莫氏篡黎，可無勘而知也，使往受謾詞辱國，請留使者毋前。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy to Annam to investigate Mo Dengyong's killing of the ruler; Yue said to Grand Coordinator Zhang Jing: "The Mo clan usurped the Le; this can be known without investigation; if the envoy goes he will receive deceitful words and disgrace the state; please detain the envoy and do not let him proceed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to Annam to investigate Mo Dengyong's murder of the ruler. Yue said to Grand Coordinator Zhang Jing, "The Mo clan usurped the Le dynasty; that much can be known without any investigation. If the envoy goes, he will only receive deceitful words and disgrace the state. Please detain the envoy and do not let him proceed.

sentences.zh: 」經不可。

translations.literal: " Jing would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Jing would not agree.

sentences.zh: 知欽州林希元上書請決討莫氏，嶽貽書止之，復條上不可討六事。

translations.literal: Lin Xiyuan, magistrate of Qinzhou, memorialized requesting a decisive campaign against the Mo clan; Yue sent a letter stopping him and also submitted in items six reasons why they should not attack.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xiyuan, magistrate of Qinzhou, memorialized requesting a decisive campaign against the Mo clan. Yue sent him a letter urging him to stop and also submitted six reasons in separate items why an attack should not be launched.

sentences.zh: 為書貽執政曰：「據邊民報，黎賙襲封無嗣，以兄子譓為子。

translations.literal: He wrote a letter to the chief ministers saying: "According to border people's reports, Le Cong inherited the seal with no son; he took his elder brother's son Hui as son.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to the chief ministers, saying, "According to reports from border people, Le Cong inherited the throne without a son of his own and adopted his elder brother's son Hui.

sentences.zh: 陳暠作亂，賙遇害，暠篡。

translations.literal: Chen Gao launched a rebellion; Cong was killed; Gao usurped.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gao launched a rebellion, Cong was killed, and Gao usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 未幾國人擁立譓，暠奔諒山。

translations.literal: Before long the people supported Hui; Gao fled to Lang Son.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the people supported Hui, and Gao fled to Lang Son.

sentences.zh: 訁惠立七年，為莫登庸所逼，出居昇華。

translations.literal: Hui ruled seven years, was forced by Mo Dengyong, and went out to live at Sinh Hoa.
translations.idiomatic: Hui ruled for seven years before Mo Dengyong forced him out to live at Sinh Hoa.

sentences.zh: 登庸立譓幼弟騑而相之，卒弑騑自立，國分為三。

translations.literal: Dengyong installed Hui's younger brother Fei and served as his prime minister; finally he assassinated Fei and set himself up; the state split into three.
translations.idiomatic: Dengyong installed Hui's younger brother Fei and served as his prime minister, then finally assassinated Fei and seized the throne himself, and the state split into three parts.

sentences.zh: 黎在南，莫居中，陳在西北。

translations.literal: The Le were in the south, the Mo in the center, and the Chen in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: The Le held the south, the Mo the center, and the Chen the northwest.

sentences.zh: 後諒山亦為登庸有，陳遂絕。

translations.literal: Later Lang Son also fell to Dengyong, and the Chen were finally extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lang Son also fell to Dengyong, and the Chen line was finally extinguished.

sentences.zh: 而黎所居即古日南地，與占城鄰，限大海，登庸不能逾之南，故兩存。

translations.literal: What the Le occupied was the ancient Rinan territory, neighboring Champa and bounded by the great sea; Dengyong could not cross south of it; hence both survived.
translations.idiomatic: The territory held by the Le was the ancient Rinan region, bordering Champa and bounded by the sea; Dengyong could not cross south of it, and so both regimes survived.

sentences.zh: 近登庸又以交州付其孫福海，而自營海東府地都齋居之。

translations.literal: Recently Dengyong again entrusted Jiaozhou to his grandson Fuhai, while himself establishing residence at Do Du in the Hai Dong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Dengyong entrusted Jiaozhou to his grandson Fuhai while establishing his own residence at Do Du in the Hai Dong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蓋安南諸府，惟海東地最大，即所謂王山郡也。

translations.literal: Of all the prefectures of Annam, only Hai Dong had the largest territory - that is the so-called Wangshan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the prefectures of Annam, Hai Dong alone had the largest territory; this was the so-called Wangshan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 此賊負篡逆名，常練兵備我，又時揚言求入貢。

translations.literal: This rebel bears the name of usurper and rebel; he constantly drills troops against us and from time to time loudly seeks to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: This rebel bears the stigma of usurpation and treason, constantly drills troops against us, and from time to time loudly professes a wish to offer tribute.

sentences.zh: 邊人以非故王也，弗敢聞。

translations.literal: Border people, because he was not the former king, dared not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was not the former king, the border people dared not report these overtures.

sentences.zh: 愚以為彼內亂未嘗有所侵犯，可且置之，待其亂定乃貢。

translations.literal: I foolishly think that while their internal chaos has not involved any invasion of us, they can be set aside for now; wait until their disorder settles and then accept tribute.
translations.idiomatic: I am inclined to think that since their internal disorder has not yet led to any invasion of our territory, the matter can be set aside for now and tribute accepted only after their turmoil has settled.

sentences.zh: 若必用兵，勝負利純非嶽所敢知。

translations.literal: If troops must be used, victory or defeat, profit or loss - Yue dares not presume to know.
translations.idiomatic: If war must be waged, the outcome, whether victory or defeat, profit or loss, is beyond what Yue dares presume to know.

sentences.zh: 」執政得書不能決。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers received the letter and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: " The chief ministers received the letter but could not reach a decision.

sentences.zh: 已，毛伯溫來視師，張經一以軍事委嶽。

translations.literal: Then Mao Bowen came to inspect the army; Zhang Jing wholly entrusted military affairs to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Then Mao Bowen came to inspect the army, and Zhang Jing wholly entrusted military affairs to Yue.

sentences.zh: 又以翁萬達才，進二人于伯溫。

translations.literal: Also because Weng Wanda had talent, he recommended both men to Bowen.
translations.idiomatic: Because Weng Wanda was also talented, he recommended both men to Bowen.

sentences.zh: 岳與伯溫語數日，伯溫曰：「交事屬君矣。

translations.literal: Yue spoke with Bowen for several days; Bowen said: "The Annam affair is yours.
translations.idiomatic: Yue spoke with Bowen for several days, and Bowen said, "The Annam affair is in your hands.

sentences.zh: 」許登庸如嶽議。

translations.literal: " He permitted Dengyong to act according to Yue's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " He allowed Dengyong to proceed according to Yue's proposal.

sentences.zh: 會嶽遷浙江提學副使，又遷參政，伯溫馳奏留之，乃改廣東參政，分守海北。

translations.literal: When Yue was transferred to vice education intendant of Zhejiang and then to administration commissioner, Bowen urgently memorialized to retain him; he was then changed to administration commissioner of Guangdong, stationed separately at Haibei.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was transferred to vice education intendant of Zhejiang and then to administration commissioner, Bowen urgently memorialized to retain him; he was then reassigned as administration commissioner of Guangdong with separate responsibility for Haibei.

sentences.zh: 登庸降，加嶽俸一級，賜銀幣。

translations.literal: When Dengyong surrendered, Yue's salary was raised one grade and silver and silks were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When Dengyong surrendered, Yue's salary was raised one grade and he was awarded silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 尋以征瓊州叛黎功，加俸及賜如之。

translations.literal: Soon for merit in campaigning against the rebel Li of Qiongzhou, salary increase and gifts were granted likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for his achievements in campaigning against the rebel Li of Qiongzhou, he received the same salary increase and gifts.

sentences.zh: 塞上多事，言官薦岳邊才。

translations.literal: The frontier was busy with affairs; remonstrating officials recommended Yue for frontier talent.
translations.idiomatic: With much trouble on the frontier, remonstrating officials recommended Yue for his frontier expertise.

sentences.zh: 伯溫言：「岳可南，翁萬達可北也。

translations.literal: Bowen said: "Yue can go south; Weng Wanda can go north.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen said, "Yue can serve in the south, and Weng Wanda can serve in the north.

sentences.zh: 」遂擢嶽右僉都御史，撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: " He was then promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Pacification Commissioner of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: " Yue was then promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed Pacification Commissioner of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 旋移撫江西，進右副都御史，總督兩廣軍務兼巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Jiangxi as grand coordinator; promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, supreme commander of the Two Guangs military affairs with concurrent grand coordinator duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Jiangxi as grand coordinator, promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and appointed supreme commander of military affairs in the Two Guangs with concurrent duties as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 討破廣東封川僮蘇公樂等，進兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He defeated the Yao of Fengchuan, Guangdong - Su Gongle and others - and was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Yao bandits of Fengchuan in Guangdong, including Su Gongle and others, and was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 平廣西馬平諸縣瑤賊，先後俘斬四千，招撫二萬餘人，誅賊魁韋金田等，增俸一級。

translations.literal: He pacified the Yao bandits in various counties including Maping, Guangxi; successively captured and beheaded four thousand, pacified and recruited more than twenty thousand; executed bandit chiefs Wei Jintian and others; salary raised one grade.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the Yao bandits in counties such as Maping in Guangxi, capturing and beheading four thousand in all, pacifying and recruiting more than twenty thousand people, executing bandit chiefs including Wei Jintian, and receiving a one-grade salary increase.

sentences.zh: 召為刑部右侍郎，以御史徐南金言命留任。

translations.literal: Summoned as Right Vice Minister of Punishments; on the memorial of censor Xu Nanjin, an order was given to remain in post.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Right Vice Minister of Punishments, but on the memorial of censor Xu Nanjin an order was issued for him to remain in his current post.

sentences.zh: 連山賊李金與賀縣賊倪仲亮等，出沒衡、永、郴、桂，積三十年不能平，嶽大合兵討擒之。

translations.literal: Bandits of Lianshan - Li Jin - and bandits of Hexian - Ni Zhongliang and others - roamed Heng, Yong, Chen, and Gui; for thirty years they could not be pacified; Yue mustered a great force and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jin, a bandit of Lianshan, and Ni Zhongliang and other bandits of Hexian had roamed Heng, Yong, Chen, and Gui for thirty years without being pacified; Yue mustered a large force and captured them.

sentences.zh: 蒞鎮四年，巨寇悉平，召拜兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: After four years at his post, all major bandits were pacified; he was summoned and appointed Left Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in command, all the major bandits had been pacified, and he was summoned and appointed Left Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 湖貴間有山曰蠟爾，諸苗居之。

translations.literal: Between Huguang and Guizhou there is a mountain called La'er; various Miao live there.
translations.idiomatic: Between Huguang and Guizhou there is a mountain called La'er where various Miao peoples live.

sentences.zh: 東屬鎮溪千戶所筸子坪長官司，隸湖廣；

translations.literal: To the east it belongs to the Gaoziping Native Official Office of Zhenxi Guard Station, under Huguang;
translations.idiomatic: To the east it belonged to the Gaoziping Native Official Office of Zhenxi Guard Station, under Huguang;

sentences.zh: 西屬銅仁、平頭二長官司，隸貴州；

translations.literal: to the west it belongs to the two native official offices of Tongren and Pingtou, under Guizhou;
translations.idiomatic: to the west to the two native official offices of Tongren and Pingtou, under Guizhou;

sentences.zh: 北接四川酉陽，廣袤數百里。

translations.literal: to the north it joins Youyang, Sichuan; hundreds of li in breadth and length.
translations.idiomatic: and to the north it bordered Youyang in Sichuan, extending hundreds of li in every direction.

sentences.zh: 諸苗數反，官兵不能制。

translations.literal: The various Miao rebelled repeatedly; government troops could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: The various Miao rebelled repeatedly, and government troops could not bring them under control.

sentences.zh: 侍郎萬鏜征之，四年不克。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Wan Yao campaigned against them; four years without success.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wan Yao campaigned against them for four years without success.

sentences.zh: 乃授其魁龍許保冠帶。

translations.literal: Thereupon they conferred upon the chieftain Long Xubao cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: The court then invested the chieftain Long Xubao with official cap and belt.

sentences.zh: 湖苗暫息，而貴苗反如故。

translations.literal: The lake-region Miao briefly subsided, but the Guizhou Miao rebelled as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao of the lake region briefly quieted, but those in Guizhou rose again as before.

sentences.zh: 鏜班師，龍許保及其党吳黑苗復亂。

translations.literal: Yao withdrew his army; Long Xubao and his follower Wu Heimiao again rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao withdrew his army, Long Xubao and his follower Wu Heimiao rose in rebellion once more.

sentences.zh: 貴州巡撫李義壯告警，乃命岳總督湖廣、貴州、四川軍務，討之。

translations.literal: Guizhou grand coordinator Li Yizhuang reported the alarm; Yue was then ordered to serve as grand coordinator of Huguang, Guizhou, and Sichuan military affairs to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When Guizhou grand coordinator Li Yizhuang sounded the alarm, Yue was appointed to oversee military affairs in Huguang, Guizhou, and Sichuan and ordered to suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 進右都御史。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 義壯持鏜議欲撫，嶽劾其阻兵，罷之。

translations.literal: Yizhuang upheld Yao's policy and wished to pacify them; Yue impeached him for obstructing military action and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhuang held to Yao's conciliation policy, but Yue impeached him for blocking the use of force and had him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 先義壯撫貴州者，僉都御史王學益與鏜附嚴嵩，主撫議，數從中撓嶽。

translations.literal: Before Yizhuang had pacified Guizhou, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Xueyi, who sided with Yao in attaching himself to Yan Song, advocated pacification and repeatedly intervened from the center to thwart Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xueyi, who had preceded Yizhuang as grand coordinator of Guizhou, had aligned with Yao and Yan Song in favor of conciliation and repeatedly undermined Yue from court.

sentences.zh: 嶽持益堅。

translations.literal: Yue held all the more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Yue held his position all the more firmly.

sentences.zh: 許保襲執印江知縣徐文伯及石阡推官鄧本忠以去，嶽坐停俸。

translations.literal: Xubao raided and seized Yinjiang magistrate Xu Wenbo and Shiqian assistant prefectural judge Deng Benzhong and carried them off; Yue was punished by salary suspension.
translations.idiomatic: Xubao raided and took captive the magistrate of Yinjiang, Xu Wenbo, and the assistant prefectural judge of Shiqian, Deng Benzhong; Yue's salary was suspended as punishment.

sentences.zh: 乃使總兵官沈希儀、參將石邦憲等分道進，躬入銅仁督之。

translations.literal: He then sent Regional Commander Shen Xiyi, Assistant Regional Commander Shi Bangxian, and others to advance by separate routes, and personally entered Tongren to direct operations.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Regional Commander Shen Xiyi and Assistant Regional Commander Shi Bangxian along separate routes, while he personally entered Tongren to direct the campaign.

sentences.zh: 先後斬賊魁五十三人，獨許保、黑苗跳不獲。

translations.literal: In succession they beheaded fifty-three bandit chiefs; only Xubao and Heimiao escaped and could not be captured.
translations.idiomatic: They successively executed fifty-three rebel chiefs, but Xubao and Heimiao alone escaped capture.

sentences.zh: 岳以捷聞，言貴苗漸平，湖苗聽撫，請遣土兵歸農，朝議許之。

translations.literal: Yue reported the victory, saying the Guizhou Miao were gradually pacified and the lake-region Miao submitted to conciliation; he requested that native troops be sent back to farming, and the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: Yue reported his victory, noting that the Guizhou Miao were being subdued and the lake-region Miao had accepted conciliation, and requested permission to send native troops back to their farms; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，酉陽宣慰冉元嗾許保、黑苗突思州，劫執知府李允簡。

translations.literal: Before long, Youyang pacification commissioner Ran Yuan instigated Xubao and Heimiao to raid Si Prefecture and seize and hold Prefect Li Yunjian.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Youyang pacification commissioner Ran Yuan incited Xubao and Heimiao to attack Si Prefecture and abduct Prefect Li Yunjian.

sentences.zh: 邦憲兵邀奪允簡還，允簡竟死。

translations.literal: Shi Bangxian's troops intercepted and recovered Yunjian, but Yunjian ultimately died.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bangxian's troops intercepted the band and recovered Yunjian, but he died in the end.

sentences.zh: 嵩父子故憾岳，欲逮治之，徐階持不可。

translations.literal: The Yan father and son bore old resentment toward Yue and wished to arrest and punish him; Xu Jie insisted this should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song and his son had long resented Yue and wanted him arrested and punished, but Xu Jie held firm against it.

sentences.zh: 乃奪右都御史，以兵部侍郎督師。

translations.literal: Thereupon his rank of Right Censor-in-Chief was stripped, and he served as Vice Minister of War directing the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of his rank as Right Censor-in-Chief and demoted to Vice Minister of War to command the army.

sentences.zh: 邦憲等旋破賊。

translations.literal: Shi Bangxian and the others soon defeated the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bangxian and the others soon broke the rebels.

sentences.zh: 岳搜山箐，餘賊獻思州印及許保。

translations.literal: Yue searched the mountain ravines; the remaining bandits presented the Si Prefecture seal and Xubao.
translations.idiomatic: Yue searched the mountain strongholds, and the remaining rebels surrendered the Si Prefecture seal along with Xubao.

sentences.zh: 湖廣兵亦破擒首惡李通海等。

translations.literal: Huguang troops also defeated and captured the chief evildoer Li Tonghai and others.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang troops also defeated and captured the ringleader Li Tonghai and others.

sentences.zh: 岳以黑苗未獲，不敢報功。

translations.literal: Because Heimiao had not been captured, Yue did not dare report meritorious achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Since Heimiao had not yet been captured, Yue did not dare claim credit for victory.

sentences.zh: 已而冉元謀露，嶽發其奸。

translations.literal: Before long Ran Yuan's plot was exposed; Yue revealed his treachery.
translations.idiomatic: When Ran Yuan's conspiracy came to light, Yue exposed his treachery.

sentences.zh: 元賄嚴世蕃責岳絕苗黨。

translations.literal: Ran bribed Yan Shifan to rebuke Yue for cutting off the Miao faction.
translations.idiomatic: Ran bribed Yan Shifan to criticize Yue for exterminating the Miao partisans.

sentences.zh: 邦憲竟得黑苗以獻，苗患乃息。

translations.literal: Shi Bangxian ultimately obtained Heimiao and presented him; the Miao trouble then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bangxian finally captured Heimiao and presented him to Yue, and the Miao unrest was ended.

sentences.zh: 岳卒於沅州。

translations.literal: Yue died at Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yue died at Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 喪歸，沅人迎哭者不絕。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned home, the people of Yuanzhou who came out to greet and weep were unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: As his coffin was borne home, the people of Yuanzhou lined the road in unbroken mourning.

sentences.zh: 已，敘功，復右都御史，贈太子少保，諡襄惠。

translations.literal: Later, merits were reviewed; his rank of Right Censor-in-Chief was restored, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and given the posthumous title Xianghui.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his merits were reviewed, his rank as Right Censor-in-Chief was restored, he was posthumously awarded the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and given the posthumous name Xianghui.

sentences.zh: 岳博覽，工文章，經術湛深，不喜王守仁學，以程、硃為宗。

translations.literal: Yue was broadly learned, skilled in literary composition, and profoundly versed in classical studies; he did not favor Wang Shouren's learning, and took Cheng and Zhu as his masters.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was widely read, adept at literary composition, and deeply grounded in classical learning; he rejected Wang Shouren's doctrines and adhered to the teachings of the Cheng-Zhu school.

sentences.zh: 李允簡，融縣人。

translations.literal: Li Yunjian was a man of Rong County.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yunjian was a native of Rong County.

sentences.zh: 由舉人起家。

translations.literal: He began his career from the juren degree.
translations.idiomatic: He entered official service through the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 以郡境多寇，道孥歸，獨與孫炳文居。

translations.literal: Because the prefecture had many bandits, he sent his wife and children home on the road, and lived alone with his grandson Sun Bingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Because bandits were rampant in the prefecture, he sent his wife and children home along the road and remained alone with his grandson Sun Bingwen.

sentences.zh: 祖孫皆被執，許保挾以求厚贖。

translations.literal: Both grandfather and grandson were seized; Xubao held them to demand a heavy ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Both grandfather and grandson were taken captive; Xubao held them hostage to extract a large ransom.

sentences.zh: 允簡則傳語邦憲令亟進兵。

translations.literal: Yunjian then sent word to Shi Bangxian ordering him to advance the army at once.
translations.idiomatic: From captivity, Yunjian sent word to Shi Bangxian urging him to advance immediately.

sentences.zh: 在賊中自投高崖下，賊拽出，棄之途。

translations.literal: While among the bandits he threw himself from a high cliff; the bandits dragged him out and abandoned him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: While in the bandits' hands he threw himself from a high cliff; the bandits pulled him out and left him by the roadside.

sentences.zh: 思人舁還，至清浪衛而卒。

translations.literal: The people of Si carried him back; he died upon reaching Qinglang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Si Prefecture carried him back, but he died upon reaching Qinglang Guard.

sentences.zh: 詔贈貴州副使，賜祭葬，官一子。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously awarded him Vice Commissioner of Guizhou, granted sacrificial rites and burial honors, and appointed one son to office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously conferred on him the rank of Vice Commissioner of Guizhou, granted him state sacrificial rites and a state funeral, and gave one son an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 郭宗皋，字君弼，福山人。

translations.literal: Guo Zonggao, styled Junbi, was a man of Fushan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zonggao, styled Junbi, was a native of Fushan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the eighth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Jiajing year 8.

sentences.zh: 選庶起士。

translations.literal: Selected as a shujishi.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a Hanlin Bachelor.

sentences.zh: 尋詔與選者皆改除，得刑部主事。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered that all those selected be reassigned; he received appointment as principal clerk of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict reassigned all those selected from the Hanlin, and he was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 擢御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 十二年十月，星隕如雨。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twelfth year, stars fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 12, meteors fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 未幾，哀沖太子薨，大同兵亂。

translations.literal: Before long Crown Prince Aichong died, and the troops at Datong mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Crown Prince Aichong died, and the garrison at Datong rose in mutiny.

sentences.zh: 宗皋勸帝惇崇寬厚，察納忠言，勿專以嚴明為治。

translations.literal: Zonggao urged the emperor to honor and esteem generosity and magnanimity, discern and accept loyal counsel, and not govern exclusively through severity and strictness.
translations.idiomatic: Zonggao urged the emperor to embrace generosity and magnanimity, heed loyal counsel, and not rely exclusively on severity as a method of rule.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，下詔獄，杖四十釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, sent him to the imperial prison, had him beaten forty strokes, and released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, had him imprisoned in the edict prison, beaten forty strokes, and then released.

sentences.zh: 曆按蘇、松、順天。

translations.literal: He successively served as investigating censor for Suzhou, Songjiang, and Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as investigating censor for Suzhou, Songjiang, and Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 行部乘馬，不禦肩輿。

translations.literal: When touring his jurisdiction he rode a horse and did not use a shoulder-borne sedan chair.
translations.idiomatic: When making the rounds of his jurisdiction he rode on horseback and refused a sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 會廷推保定巡撫劉夔還理院事，宗皋論夔嘗薦大學士李時子，諂媚無行，不任風紀，坐奪俸兩月。

translations.literal: When the court nominated Baoding grand coordinator Liu Kui to return and administer the Censorate, Zonggao argued that Kui had once recommended the son of Grand Secretary Li Shi, was fawning and without conduct, and was unfit for censorial discipline; he was punished by two months' salary deduction.
translations.idiomatic: When the court nominated Baoding grand coordinator Liu Kui to return and head the Censorate, Zonggao charged that Kui had once recommended the son of Grand Secretary Li Shi, was obsequious and corrupt, and unfit to uphold censorial standards; for this Zonggao was punished with two months' suspension of salary.

sentences.zh: 尋出為雁門兵備副使，轉陝西參政，遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as vice commissioner of the Yanmen military defense circuit, transferred to administration commissioner of Shaanxi, and moved to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted as vice commissioner for the Yanmen defense circuit, transferred to administration commissioner of Shaanxi, and promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 二十三年十月，寇入萬全右衛，抵廣昌，列營四十里。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-third year, raiders entered Wanquan Right Guard, reached Guangchang, and encamped in a line forty li long.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 23, raiders entered Wanquan Right Guard, advanced to Guangchang, and pitched camp in a forty-li line.

sentences.zh: 順天巡撫硃方下獄，擢宗皋右僉都御史代之，寇已去。

translations.literal: Shuntian grand coordinator Zhu Fang was imprisoned; Zonggao was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to replace him, but the raiders had already departed.
translations.idiomatic: Shuntian grand coordinator Zhu Fang was thrown into prison, and Zonggao was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to replace him, by which time the raiders had already withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 宗皋言：「密雲最要害，宜宿重兵。

translations.literal: Zonggao said: "Miyun is the most critical point and ought to station heavy troops there.
translations.idiomatic: Zonggao memorialized: "Miyun is the most critical point and should be garrisoned with substantial forces.

sentences.zh: 乞敕馬蘭、太平、燕河三屯歲發千人，以五月赴密雲，有警則總兵官自將赴援。

translations.literal: I beg that an order be issued for the three garrisons of Malan, Taiping, and Yanhe to dispatch a thousand men each year in the fifth month to Miyun; when there is an alarm the regional commander himself shall lead troops to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: I request that the three garrisons of Malan, Taiping, and Yanhe be ordered to send a thousand men each year in the fifth month to Miyun, and that when alarm arises the regional commander himself should lead reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 居庸、白楊，地要兵弱，遇警必待部奏，不能及事。

translations.literal: Juyong and Baiyang are vital ground but weak in troops; when alarm arises one must await memorials from the ministry and cannot meet the emergency in time.
translations.idiomatic: Juyong and Baiyang are strategically vital but weakly garrisoned; in an emergency troops cannot be moved in time because one must wait for approval from the ministry.

sentences.zh: 請預擬借調之法，令建昌三屯軍，平時則協助密雲，遇警則移駐居庸。

translations.literal: I request a method of advance planning for borrowing and transferring troops, so that the armies of the three Jianchang garrisons may assist Miyun in normal times and be shifted to garrison Juyong when alarm arises.
translations.idiomatic: I propose prearranged transfer arrangements under which the three Jianchang garrisons would support Miyun in peacetime and redeploy to Juyong when alarm arises.

sentences.zh: 」俱報可。

translations.literal: " All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: " All proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 久之，宗皋聞敵騎四十萬欲分道入，奏調京營、山東、河南兵為援。

translations.literal: After some time, Zonggao heard that four hundred thousand enemy horsemen intended to enter by separate routes; he memorialized requesting troops from the capital garrisons, Shandong, and Henan as reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Zonggao heard reports that four hundred thousand enemy horsemen were preparing to invade by separate routes, and he memorialized requesting reinforcements from the capital garrisons, Shandong, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 已竟無實，坐奪俸一年。

translations.literal: It ultimately proved groundless; he was punished by one year's salary suspension.
translations.idiomatic: The report proved entirely false, and he was punished with one year's suspension of salary.

sentences.zh: 故事，京營歲發五軍詣薊鎮防秋。

translations.literal: By precedent, the capital garrisons each year sent the Five Armies to Ji Town for autumn defense.
translations.idiomatic: By established practice, the capital garrisons each year dispatched the Five Armies to Ji Town for autumn defense.

sentences.zh: 宗皋請罷三軍，以其犒軍銀充本鎮募兵費。

translations.literal: Zonggao requested abolishing three armies and using their troop-reward silver to cover local recruitment costs for the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Zonggao requested that three of the armies be discontinued and their reward funds used to cover local recruitment costs for the garrison.

sentences.zh: 又請發修邊餘銀，增築燕河營、古北口。

translations.literal: He also requested disbursing surplus silver from border repairs to build up the Yanhe camp and Gubeikou.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested that surplus funds from border repairs be used to strengthen the Yanhe camp and Gubeikou.

sentences.zh: 帝疑有侵冒，令罷歸聽勘。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected embezzlement, ordered him dismissed and returned to face investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected corruption and ordered him dismissed and sent home pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 既而事得白。

translations.literal: Before long the matter was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was cleared of wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 起故官，巡撫大同，與宣府巡撫李仁易鎮。

translations.literal: He was restored to his former post, served as grand coordinator of Datong, and exchanged posts with Xuanfu grand coordinator Li Ren.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to office, appointed grand coordinator of Datong, and exchanged posts with Li Ren, grand coordinator of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 尋進兵部右侍郎，總督宣、大、山西軍務。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Right Vice Minister of War and served as grand coordinator of Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Vice Minister of War and appointed grand coordinator of military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 俺答三萬騎犯萬全左衛，總兵官陳鳳、副總兵林椿與戰鷂兒嶺，殺傷相當，宗皋坐奪俸。

translations.literal: Altan led thirty thousand horsemen to invade Wanquan Left Guard; Regional Commander Chen Feng and Vice Regional Commander Lin Chun fought them at Yaor Ling with roughly equal casualties; Zonggao was punished by salary suspension.
translations.idiomatic: Altan invaded Wanquan Left Guard with thirty thousand horsemen; Regional Commander Chen Feng and Vice Regional Commander Lin Chun engaged them at Yaor Ling with roughly equal losses on both sides, and Zonggao's salary was suspended as punishment.

sentences.zh: 明年再犯大同，總兵官張達及椿皆戰死，宗皋與巡撫陳燿坐奪俸。

translations.literal: The next year they invaded Datong again; Regional Commander Zhang Da and Lin Chun both died in battle; Zonggao and grand coordinator Chen Yao were punished by salary suspension.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the raiders struck Datong again; Regional Commander Zhang Da and Lin Chun were both killed in battle, and the salaries of Zonggao and grand coordinator Chen Yao were suspended.

sentences.zh: 給事中唐禹追論死事狀，因言全軍悉陷，乃數十年未有之大衄。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Tang Yu reviewed the circumstances of those who died in battle and stated that the entire army had been lost — a defeat unmatched in decades.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Tang Yu reviewed the circumstances of the fallen and declared that the entire army had been annihilated — a catastrophe unmatched in decades.

sentences.zh: 帝乃逮宗皋及燿，各杖一百，燿遂死，宗皋戍陝西靖虜衛。

translations.literal: The emperor then arrested Zonggao and Yao, had each beaten one hundred strokes; Yao then died, and Zonggao was banished to Jinglu Guard in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then had Zonggao and Yao arrested and beaten one hundred strokes each; Yao died from the beating, and Zonggao was exiled to Jinglu Guard in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 隆慶改元，從戍所起刑部右侍郎，改兵部，協理戎政。

translations.literal: At the change of reign era to Longqing, he was raised from exile to Right Vice Minister of Justice, transferred to the Ministry of War, and assigned to assist in military administration.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign he was recalled from exile as Right Vice Minister of Justice, transferred to the Ministry of War, and charged with assisting in military administration.

sentences.zh: 旋進南京右都御史，就改兵部尚書參贊機務。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing, and then changed to Minister of War assisting in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing, then transferred to Minister of War with a role in state council deliberations.

sentences.zh: 給事中莊國禎劾宗皋衰庸，宗皋亦自以年老求去，詔許之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhuang Guozhen impeached Zonggao as decrepit and incompetent; Zonggao also, considering himself old, requested retirement, and an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhuang Guozhen impeached Zonggao as senile and incompetent; Zonggao, finding himself too old to serve, also requested retirement, and the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，再存問，歲給廩隸。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign he was again sent inquiries of concern, and granted yearly stipends and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign the court twice sent envoys to inquire after him and granted him an annual stipend and attendants.

sentences.zh: 十六年，宗皋年九十，又遣行人存問。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, when Zonggao was ninety, envoys were again dispatched to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16, when Zonggao reached ninety, the court again dispatched a palace emissary to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 是年卒。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，諡康介。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Kangjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Kangjie.

sentences.zh: 趙時春，字景仁，平涼人。

translations.literal: Zhao Shichun, styled Jingren, was a man of Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shichun, styled Jingren, was a native of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 幼與群兒嬉，輒列旗幟，部勒如兵法。

translations.literal: As a child, when playing with other boys he would array banners and flags and drill them according to military method.
translations.idiomatic: As a child, when playing with other boys he would set up banners and drill them as if by the art of war.

sentences.zh: 年十四舉於鄉。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 逾四年，為嘉靖五年，會試第一。

translations.literal: After four more years, in the fifth year of Jiajing, he ranked first in the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later, in Jiajing year 5, he ranked first in the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 選庶起士。

translations.literal: Selected as a shujishi.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a Hanlin Bachelor.

sentences.zh: 以張璁言改官，得戶部主事。

translations.literal: On Zhang Cong's recommendation his appointment was changed, and he received appointment as principal clerk of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhang Cong's recommendation he was reassigned and appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋轉兵部。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，上疏曰：「陛下以災變求言已旬月，大小臣工率浮詞面謾。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year he submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has sought advice on calamities and portents for a full month already, yet officials great and small mostly offer empty words and face-to-face deceit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 9 he submitted a memorial, saying, "Your Majesty has sought counsel regarding calamities and portents for a full month, yet officials high and low have mostly offered empty words and face-to-face flattery.

sentences.zh: 蓋自靈寶知縣言河清受賞，都御史汪鋐繼進甘露，今副都御史徐贊、訓導范仲斌進瑞麥，指揮張楫進嘉禾，鋐及御史楊東又進鹽華，禮部尚書李時再請表賀。

translations.literal: Since the magistrate of Lingbao spoke of the river clearing and received reward, Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong subsequently presented sweet dew; now Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Zan and instructor Fan Zhongbin presented auspicious wheat, Commander Zhang Ji presented fine grain, Hong and censor Yang Dong again presented salt flowers, and Minister of Rites Li Shi again requested congratulatory proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the magistrate of Lingbao was rewarded for reporting that the Yellow River had run clear, Censor-in-Chief Wang Hong presented sweet dew; now Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Zan and instructor Fan Zhongbin have presented auspicious wheat, Commander Zhang Ji has presented fine grain, Hong and Censor Yang Dong have presented salt flowers, and Minister of Rites Li Shi has again requested a formal congratulatory address.

sentences.zh: 仲斌等不足道，鋐、贊司風紀，時典三禮，乃罔上欺君，壞風傷政。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongbin and the like are not worth mentioning, but Hong and Zan oversee censorial discipline, and Shi presides over the three rites — yet they deceive the sovereign above and ruin customs and harm governance.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Fan Zhongbin are beneath notice, but Hong and Zan oversee censorial discipline and Shi presides over the three rites — yet they deceive the throne, corrupt public morals, and damage governance.

sentences.zh: 」帝責其妄言，且令獻讜言善策。

translations.literal: " The emperor rebuked him for reckless speech and also ordered him to submit loyal advice and good plans.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor rebuked him for reckless speech and ordered him to submit loyal counsel and sound policies.

sentences.zh: 時春惶恐引咎未對。

translations.literal: Shichun, fearful, acknowledged guilt and had not yet replied.
translations.idiomatic: Shichun, filled with alarm, accepted blame but had not yet responded.

sentences.zh: 帝趣之，於是時春上言：

translations.literal: The emperor pressed him, and thereupon Shichun submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor pressed him, Shichun submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 當今之務最大者有四，最急者有三。

translations.literal: Of present tasks the greatest are four, and the most urgent are three.
translations.idiomatic: Among present priorities, four are greatest and three are most urgent.

sentences.zh: 最大者，曰崇治本。

translations.literal: Of the greatest, the first is to honor the foundation of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Of the greatest priorities, the first is to honor the foundations of governance.

sentences.zh: 君之喜怒，賞罰所自出，勿以逆心事為可怒，則賞罰大公而天下治。

translations.literal: The ruler's pleasure and anger are the source from which rewards and punishments proceed; do not treat unwelcome matters as grounds for anger, and then rewards and punishments will be utterly fair and the realm will be well governed.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's moods are the wellspring of rewards and punishments; do not treat unwelcome truths as cause for anger, and rewards and punishments will be just and the realm well governed.

sentences.zh: 曰信號令。

translations.literal: The second is to trust commands and orders.
translations.idiomatic: The second is to uphold the credibility of commands.

sentences.zh: 無信一人之言，必參諸公論；

translations.literal: Do not trust the word of one man alone; one must consult general opinion;
translations.idiomatic: Do not rely on the word of a single person; weigh all informed opinion;

sentences.zh: 毋狃一時之近，必稽之永遠。

translations.literal: do not cling to what is near in the moment; one must examine what holds over the long term.
translations.idiomatic: do not fixate on immediate advantage; measure policies by their lasting effects.

sentences.zh: 苟利十而害一，則利不必興；

translations.literal: If benefit is ten but harm is one, then the benefit need not be undertaken;
translations.idiomatic: If a policy yields ten parts gain and one part harm, the gain is not worth pursuing;

sentences.zh: 功百而費半，則功不必舉。

translations.literal: if achievement is a hundred but cost is half, then the achievement need not be launched.
translations.idiomatic: if a project yields a hundred parts benefit but consumes half as much again in cost, it is still not worth undertaking.

sentences.zh: 如是而天下享安靜之福矣。

translations.literal: Thus the realm will enjoy the blessing of peace and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the realm will enjoy lasting peace and stability.

sentences.zh: 曰廣延訪。

translations.literal: The third is to broaden consultation.
translations.idiomatic: The third is to broaden consultation.

sentences.zh: 宜仿古人輪對及我朝宣召之制，使大臣、台諫、侍從各得敷納殿陛間，群吏則以其職事召問之。

translations.literal: One ought to follow the ancient system of rotating audience and our dynasty's summons to court, so that grand secretaries, censorate remonstrators, and attendants may each present and offer counsel in the hall, while officials of various ranks are summoned and questioned according to their duties.
translations.idiomatic: The court should revive the ancient practice of rotating audiences and the Ming custom of imperial summons, so that ministers, censorial remonstrators, and attendants may each speak freely before the throne, while officials at large are summoned to account for their duties.

sentences.zh: 曰勵廉恥。

translations.literal: The fourth is to encourage integrity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth is to nurture integrity and a sense of shame.

sentences.zh: 大臣宜待以禮，取大節略小過。

translations.literal: Grand ministers ought to be treated with propriety; take the major integrity and overlook minor faults.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers should be treated with respect; weigh their essential loyalty and overlook minor faults.

sentences.zh: 台諫言是者用之，非者寬容之。

translations.literal: When censorate remonstrators speak correctly, employ them; when wrong, be tolerant toward them.
translations.idiomatic: When censorial remonstrators speak rightly, heed them; when they are wrong, treat them with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 庶臣工自愛，不敢不勵。

translations.literal: Thus officials will value themselves and dare not fail to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In this way officials will value their honor and exert themselves without need of compulsion.

sentences.zh: 其最急者，曰惜人才。

translations.literal: Of the most urgent, the first is to cherish human talent.
translations.idiomatic: Of the most urgent priorities, the first is to preserve human talent.

sentences.zh: 凡得罪諸臣，其才不當棄，其過或可原，宜霈然發命，召還故秩。

translations.literal: Of all officials who have offended, their talent ought not be cast away; their faults may be pardonable — one ought to issue a sweeping decree summoning them back to their former ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who have fallen from favor should not have their talents discarded; their faults may be pardonable. A generous decree should restore them to their former offices.

sentences.zh: 且因南郊禮成，除謫戍之罪，與之更始。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the southern suburban sacrifice is completed, remit the punishments of banishment and frontier service and grant them a fresh start.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the southern suburban rites are completed, remit the penalties of exile and frontier service and give them a fresh start.

sentences.zh: 曰固邊圉。

translations.literal: The second is to secure the borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: The second is to secure the borderlands.

sentences.zh: 敗軍之律宜嚴，臨陣而退者，裨將得以戮士卒，大將得以戮裨將，總制官得以戮大將，則人心震悚，而所向用命。

translations.literal: Laws for defeated armies ought to be strict: one who retreats before the battle line — the vice commander may execute soldiers, the regional commander may execute vice commanders, and the supreme commander may execute regional commanders; then hearts will be struck with fear and all will obey their orders.
translations.idiomatic: The laws governing defeated armies should be strict: when troops retreat in battle, vice commanders should be empowered to execute soldiers, regional commanders to execute vice commanders, and supreme commanders to execute regional commanders. This would strike fear into every heart and make all obey their orders.

sentences.zh: 曰正治教。

translations.literal: The third is to rectify governance and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The third is to rectify governance and moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 請復古冠婚、喪祭之禮，絕醮祭、禱祀之術。

translations.literal: I request restoring the ancient rites of capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice, and cutting off the practices of spirit offerings and prayer rites.
translations.idiomatic: I request restoring the ancient rites of capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice, and putting an end to spirit offerings and prayer rituals.

sentences.zh: 凡佛老之徒有假引符籙、依託經懺、幻化黃白、飛升遐景以冒寵祿者，即賜遣斥，則正道修明而民志定。

translations.literal: All followers of Buddhism and Daoism who falsely cite talismans, rely on scripture repentance, conjure gold and silver, or claim ascent to distant realms to win favor and emolument — immediately dismiss and banish them; then the right path will be cultivated and bright and the people's will be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Any Buddhist or Daoist who falsely claims magical talismans, performs scripture-based penance, pretends to transmute gold and silver, or claims to ascend to immortality in order to win favor and office should immediately be dismissed and banished. In this way the right path will be maintained and the people's convictions will be settled.

sentences.zh: 帝覽之，益怒，下詔獄掠治，黜為民。

translations.literal: The emperor reviewed it, grew angrier still, sent him to prison under edict for interrogation by torture, and dismissed him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial, grew even angrier, and had him thrown into prison for interrogation under torture, then dismissed to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 久之，選東宮官屬，起翰林編修兼司經局校書。

translations.literal: After some time, when selecting Eastern Palace officials, he was raised as Hanlin Compiler, also serving as collator of the Classics Collation Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, when selecting Eastern Palace officials, he was recalled as Hanlin Compiler and concurrently appointed collator of the Classics Collation Bureau.

sentences.zh: 帝有疾，時春與羅洪先、唐順之疏請東宮禦殿，受百官正旦朝賀。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell ill, Shichun together with Luo Hongxian and Tang Shunzhi submitted a memorial requesting that the crown prince preside in the hall and receive the officials' New Year's Day court audience.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, Shichun, Luo Hongxian, and Tang Shunzhi submitted a memorial requesting that the crown prince preside in the palace hall and receive the officials' New Year's Day court audience.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，復黜為民。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and again dismissed him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and again dismissed him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 京師被寇，朝議以時春知兵，起兵部主事，贊理京營務，統民兵訓練。

translations.literal: When the capital was raided, court discussion held that Shichun understood military affairs; he was raised as principal clerk of the Ministry of War, assigned to assist in managing capital garrison affairs, and put in charge of training militia.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders struck the capital, the court decided that Shichun understood military affairs; he was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of War to assist in managing capital garrison affairs and placed in charge of training militia.

sentences.zh: 大將軍仇鸞倡馬市，時春憤曰：「此秦檜續耳。

translations.literal: The grand general Qiu Luan advocated the horse market; Shichun said angrily: "This is but a continuation of Qin Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Qiu Luan advocated establishing a horse market. Shichun said angrily, "This is nothing but a revival of Qin Hui's policy.

sentences.zh: 身為大將，而效市儈，可乎？

translations.literal: Being a grand general yet acting like a street peddler — is this acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: To hold the rank of grand general yet behave like a market huckster — is that acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 」忤鸞，為所構，幾重得罪。

translations.literal: " He offended Qiu and was framed by him, nearly incurring serious punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He offended Qiu and was framed by him, nearly incurring serious punishment again.

sentences.zh: 稍遷山東僉事，進副使。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to Shandong Assistant Commissioner, then advanced to Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually transferred to Shandong Assistant Commissioner and then promoted to Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，擢僉都御史，巡撫山西。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief and served as grand coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 32 he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 時春慷慨負奇氣，善騎射。

translations.literal: Shichun was magnanimous and possessed extraordinary spirit; he was skilled at horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Shichun was bold-spirited and possessed of unusual confidence; he was skilled in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 慨寇縱橫，將帥不任職，數謂人：「使吾領選卒五千，俺答、邱福不足平也。

translations.literal: Lamenting that raiders ranged freely and generals failed in their duties, he often told people: "If I were to lead five thousand picked troops, Altan and Qiu Fu would be nothing difficult to subdue.
translations.idiomatic: Grieved that raiders ranged freely while commanders failed in their duties, he often told people, "If I were given command of five thousand picked troops, Altan and Qiu Fu would be easy to subdue.

sentences.zh: 」作《禦寇論》，論戰守甚悉。

translations.literal: " He composed On Repelling Raiders, discussing offense and defense very thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: " He wrote On Repelling Raiders, setting forth offense and defense in great detail.

sentences.zh: 既秉節鉞，益思以武功自奮。

translations.literal: Once he held the commander's tally and axe, he all the more resolved to distinguish himself through military achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held military command, he was all the more determined to distinguish himself on the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，寇入神池、利民諸堡，時春率馬步兵往禦之。

translations.literal: That year in the ninth month raiders entered the forts of Shenchi, Limin, and others; Shichun led cavalry and infantry to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: That September raiders entered the forts of Shenchi, Limin, and elsewhere; Shichun led cavalry and infantry to repel them.

sentences.zh: 至廣武，諸將畢會。

translations.literal: Arriving at Guangwu, all the generals assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Guangwu, he assembled all the generals.

sentences.zh: 謀報寇騎二千餘，去兩舍。

translations.literal: Spies reported more than two thousand enemy horsemen, two stages away.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence reported more than two thousand enemy horsemen, about sixty li away.

sentences.zh: 時春擐甲欲馳，大將李淶固止之。

translations.literal: Shichun donned armor and wished to gallop forth; Grand General Li Lai firmly stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Shichun armored himself and prepared to charge; Grand General Li Lai firmly restrained him.

sentences.zh: 時春大言曰：「賊知吾來必遁，緩追即不及。

translations.literal: Shichun spoke boldly: "The bandits, knowing I have come, will surely flee; if pursuit is delayed they cannot be overtaken.
translations.idiomatic: Shichun declared boldly, "Once the bandits know I have arrived they will surely flee; delay pursuit and we will never catch them.

sentences.zh: 」遂策馬前。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he spurred his horse forward.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he spurred his horse forward.

sentences.zh: 及於大蟲嶺，伏兵四起，敗績。

translations.literal: Reaching Dachong Ridge, ambush troops rose on all sides, and they suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At Dachong Ridge ambushers sprang up on every side, and the force was routed.

sentences.zh: 倉皇投一墩，守卒縋之上乃得免，淶軍竟覆。

translations.literal: In panic he rushed to a signal tower; the garrison soldiers lowered a rope and pulled him up before he escaped; Li Lai's army was utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In panic he fled to a signal tower; the garrison soldiers lowered a rope and hauled him up, and only thus did he escape; Li Lai's army was entirely destroyed.

sentences.zh: 被論，解官聽調。

translations.literal: He was impeached, dismissed from office, and awaited reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached, he was dismissed from office and held pending reassignment.

sentences.zh: 時春喜談兵，至是一戰而敗。

translations.literal: Shichun loved to discuss military affairs, but now one battle brought defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Shichun had always loved to talk of military affairs, yet here one engagement brought defeat.

sentences.zh: 然當是時將帥率避寇不擊。

translations.literal: Yet at that time generals mostly avoided raiders and did not attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at that time commanders generally avoided the raiders and refused to engage.

sentences.zh: 為督撫者安居堅城，遙領軍事，無躬搏寇者。

translations.literal: Those serving as grand coordinators lived securely in strong cities, directed military affairs from afar, and none personally grappled with raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Governors and coordinators sat safely in fortified cities, directing military affairs from a distance; none personally engaged the raiders.

sentences.zh: 時春功雖不就，天下皆壯其氣。

translations.literal: Though Shichun's achievement did not succeed, all under Heaven admired his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shichun's campaign failed, people throughout the realm admired his courage.

sentences.zh: 時春讀書善強記，文章豪肆，與唐順之、王慎中齊名。

translations.literal: Shichun was skilled at reading and had a strong memory; his prose was bold and unrestrained, and he was ranked equal with Tang Shunzhi and Wang Shenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Shichun read widely and had an excellent memory; his prose was bold and expansive, and he ranked among the leading literati alongside Tang Shunzhi and Wang Shenzhong.

sentences.zh: 詩，伉浪自喜類其為人。

translations.literal: In poetry he was proud and unrestrained, delighting in himself — like his character.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was equally bold and self-assured, much like the man himself.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：姚鏌等封疆宣其擘畫，軍務暢其機謀，勳績咸有可紀。

translations.literal: The encomium states: Yao Mo and the others at the frontiers displayed their plans, in military affairs their stratagems flowed freely, and their achievements all merit record.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium states: Yao Mo and his colleagues distinguished themselves on the frontiers through their planning; in military affairs their stratagems proved effective, and their achievements all merit record.

sentences.zh: 伍文定從王守仁平宸濠之難，厥功最懋。

translations.literal: Wu Wending followed Wang Shouren in pacifying the Prince of Ning rebellion; his merit was the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wending followed Wang Shouren in suppressing the Prince of Ning rebellion; his achievement was the greatest of them all.

sentences.zh: 趙時春將略自命，一出輒躓。

translations.literal: Zhao Shichun deemed himself a strategist, yet at his first venture he stumbled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shichun fancied himself a strategist, yet his first campaign ended in defeat.

sentences.zh: 夫危事而易言之，固知兵者所弗取乎。

translations.literal: To speak lightly of dangerous matters — is this not what those who truly understand warfare refuse to do?
translations.idiomatic: To speak lightly of grave affairs — is that not precisely what those who truly understand warfare refuse to do?
